rooms.name: Rope Market
rooms.description: The floating stalls are tied to rings at three different heights. The rope sellers never agree which ring to trust.

encounters.cue: Compare the wear inside the three rings.
encounters.result: Only the middle ring is polished all the way round. The other two were for tying up in a hurry when the lake moved.

rooms.name: Ferry Steps
rooms.description: Iven chalks the safe draught on his gunwale. Across the lake, lanterns hang under the far pier like yellow fruit.

encounters.cue: Iven the ferryman folds each fare into his cuff. He fears losing the crossing that feeds both banks.
encounters.result: Iven promises boats for the evacuation once the pilot bell calls both crews. A permanent drawdown would turn his working lake into a footpath.

replies.text: Iven measures the mud with his oar. He wants the new road to follow the old ferry course, right down to the last turn.
Iven ferries doors for free. He tells you he can charge fares again once the families are under a roof.
Iven shows you the new fare card: keepers on shift cross free from either bank.

Iven poles against bare mud. He points to the cut in the white bank where the salt rail has emerged. FILL at the trial weir will float him again. He promises his crew will help the borough families once the shift bell calls.

changes.text: The water has pulled away. Iven’s ferry rests on its keel, the crossing shut; the road through the works remains dry.
The ferry floats between the steps and far pier at a taut rope’s length.
Iven lays his longest oar on the mud to measure out a road. His first passengers on foot carry shoes for the walk.
Iven chalks a fare of zero for families carrying a salvaged door. His boat rides low on a full lake.
Iven takes both gate crews across together. The boat rides high enough for a load of bread as well.

rooms.name: Net Loft
rooms.description: Knotted net patterns make family names that can be read in the dark with a fingertip.

encounters.cue: Feel where two family patterns meet.
encounters.result: The join repeats the last knot of each name. A repaired net remembered both the maker and the mender.

rooms.name: Blue Slip
rooms.description: A painted cradle fits exactly one boat. Blue paint comes away on wet fingers.

encounters.cue: Look at the oldest paint under the cradle.
encounters.result: Below the blue lies a coat of red with a child's palm in it. The palm would have been under the keel at every launch.

rooms.name: Oar Orchard
rooms.description: Spare oars stand blade-up in tubs of sand. Each blade carries a child's measured height.

encounters.cue: Compare the height marks on two oars.
encounters.result: A short notch continues onto the next blade with the same date. The child had outgrown an oar before the family could spare a doorpost.

rooms.name: Tar Cauldron
rooms.description: Lake pitch cooks over a covered flame. A ladle rests beside instructions for sealing a ferry in under a minute.

encounters.cue: Inspect the lip of the pitch ladle.
encounters.result: One side has a narrow spout for seams. The wide side could lay a patch over a split plank in a single pour.

rooms.name: Market Raft
rooms.description: The scales are hung from the ceiling so the rocking of the raft cannot favour either trader.

encounters.cue: Follow the cord below the scales.
encounters.result: A stone on a cord hangs beside a painted line. Both traders could see when the raft was level enough to weigh a loaf.

rooms.name: Mussel Wall
rooms.description: A streak of dead shells records the last drawdown. New white shells have only just reached a hand's width above it.

encounters.cue: Compare shells at the two edges of the dead band.
encounters.result: At the top the shells are shut tight. At the bottom they opened in place, long after the first ones had dried.

rooms.name: Cradle Jetty
rooms.description: A box on a pulley carried babies between the quay and the boat when the steps were submerged.

encounters.cue: Examine the cleat beside the cradle line.
encounters.result: There is a second, much smaller handgrip alongside it. An older child could steady the box for a younger one.

rooms.name: Far Pier
rooms.description: A brass bell faces Iven's ferry across the water. A landward stair climbs to the lantern borough.

changes.text: The water has pulled away. Iven’s ferry rests on its keel, the crossing shut; the road through the works remains dry.
The ferry floats between the steps and far pier at a taut rope’s length.

encounters.cue: Inspect the shore bell's clapper.
encounters.result: Leather covers half the clapper. A keeper could call across the water without waking the houses behind the pier.

rooms.name: Sail Hospital
rooms.description: Old sailcloth divides the cots. A stitched red line tells a nurse where to stand when the floor floats free.

encounters.cue: Trace the seam along a sailcloth screen.
encounters.result: Buttonholes are stitched into the lower hem. Two poles would turn the screen into a stretcher without lifting a patient.

rooms.name: Bottle Beach
rooms.description: Each sealed bottle contains a fare paid by a passenger who meant to come back.

encounters.cue: Look through the glass at the fares.
encounters.result: One passenger left a coat button with a fare inked on the back. The ferryman accepted a promise small enough to wear.

rooms.name: Keel Shrine
rooms.description: Half a sunken keel shelters the names of crews who drowned bringing bread to the lower shore.

encounters.cue: Examine the wooden pegs among the names.
encounters.result: Each peg carries a cut shaped like a loaf. Smooth hollows beneath show where fresh bread once rested.

rooms.name: Chain Buoy
rooms.description: A bell buoy hangs from a ceiling chain. When the lake rises it loses its voice.

encounters.cue: Inspect the tongue inside the bell buoy.
encounters.result: A cork collar lifts the tongue clear of the bell before the rim goes under. The buoy's silence was itself an alarm.

rooms.name: Ferry Ledger
rooms.description: Fares are entered as favours. One whole bank of the lake owes Iven exactly one dry night.

encounters.cue: Read the marks in the margin of the fare book.
encounters.result: A night spent holding a mooring line earned the same tally as a night sheltering a passenger.

rooms.name: Reed Screen
rooms.description: Wind passes through hollow reeds in single notes. A broad gap once let the ferry mast pass.

encounters.cue: Examine the bindings beside the mast gap.
encounters.result: Two cords have quick-release loops at deck height. The crew could open the screen from a boat without cutting a reed.

rooms.name: Sounding Post
rooms.description: Wet knots at uneven intervals mark the depth under the landing. A fresh knot is still white.

encounters.cue: Feel the newest knot in the sounding line.
encounters.result: A slim lead weight is tucked into its centre. It keeps that reading distinct from the others even in fog.

rooms.name: Eel Smokehouse
rooms.description: The smoke draws toward a crack in the far cliff. Warm air from the pottery kilns leaks back through it.

encounters.cue: Examine the hooks nearest the warm crack.
encounters.result: The last three carry strips of damp cloth. Their drying time told the smoker when the kilns were drawing well.

rooms.name: Beach Winch
rooms.description: The winch rope loops around a stone shaped like a knuckle. It could hold the ferry upright on mud.

changes.text: The water has pulled away. Iven’s ferry rests on its keel, the crossing shut; the road through the works remains dry.
The ferry floats between the steps and far pier at a taut rope’s length.

encounters.cue: Look at the chock under the winch drum.
encounters.result: Someone shaped it from an old oar grip. A thumb groove gives purchase when the rope pulls tight.

rooms.name: Pilot's Lamp
rooms.description: Two wicks burn at different heights, one for boatmen and one for travellers on the high road.

encounters.cue: Look behind the two pilot flames.
encounters.result: One reflector is angled down, the other up. A traveller climbing from a boat can see one light hand them over to the next.

links.obstacle: The water is too low for the ferry. Its hull rests on mud.
links.hint: Refill the lake at the trial weir or go around via the works.
